q: Real-time Updates 模式主要解决什么问题？
q_en: What problem does the Real-time Updates pattern solve?
options: 客户端如何把大文件分片上传到对象存储并支持断点续传
事件发生后，服务器如何用低延迟把状态变化推送给已连接的客户端
数据库如何用 B-tree 索引加速范围查询
静态 HTML/CSS 资源如何压缩后经 CDN 分发给用户
why: 实时更新的核心是服务器主动推送状态变化，而不是客户端反复拉取或询问；关注低延迟和推送两件事。
why_en: Real-time updates deliver server-side events or data changes to clients with low latency.
options_en: How the client uploads a large file to object storage in chunks with resume support.
How the server pushes state changes to already-connected clients with low latency after something happens.
How a database uses a B-tree index to speed up range queries.
How static HTML and CSS assets are compressed and served through a CDN.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点的网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a network of edge servers that caches content close to users.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库常用的平衡树索引结构，用于加速范围查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a balanced tree index structure that speeds up database range queries.

optionExplanations: 这是文件上传/断点续传的问题，跟服务器主动推送状态变化无关。
抓住了核心：事件发生后由服务器主动、低延迟地把变化推给已连接客户端。
这是数据库查询加速，属于存储层优化，不是推送问题。
这是静态资源分发，CDN 缓存的是不变内容，不解决状态变化推送。
optionExplanations_en: That describes chunked upload and resume, not server-initiated push of state changes.
Nails it: after something happens, the server proactively pushes the change to already-connected clients with low latency.
That's a database indexing concern for range queries, not a push problem.
That's static asset distribution through a CDN, which caches unchanging content instead of pushing changes.
scenario: 你在做体育比分直播页：比分一变，所有在线观众 1 秒内要看到，且不用刷新页面。
scenario_en: You're building a live sports scoreboard page: when the score changes, every online viewer should see it within a second without refreshing.

q: 实时更新设计通常要分别解决哪两个 hop？（多选）
q_en: Which two hops does a realtime update design usually need to solve? (Select all that apply.)
options: server 到 client 的连接协议
事件源到负责连接的 server 的传播方式
如何把 JavaScript 编译成机器码
如何给图片生成缩略图
why: 第一跳是 client-server 协议选型；第二跳是更新如何从产生处传播到持有连接的 server；两跳取舍相互独立。
why_en: Real-time design has two hops: client-server delivery and source-to-server update propagation.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["事件源"] -->|hop 1| B["连接服务器"]
    B -->|hop 2| C["客户端"]
    D["协议选择"] -.-> B
    E["传播方式"] -.-> A
options_en: The connection protocol between server and client.
How updates propagate from their source to the server holding the connection.
How to compile JavaScript down to machine code.
How to generate thumbnails for images.

termDefinitions.meaning: 更新在到达客户端路上要经过的一段传输环节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hop is one leg of the path an update travels on its way to the client.

optionExplanations: 第一跳：client 和负责连接的 server 之间用什么协议通信，是 polling 还是 WebSocket 这类选择。
第二跳：更新产生的地方要传播到持有连接的那台 server，常靠 pub/sub 或路由完成。
这是前端构建/编译问题，跟第一跳还是第二跳都扯不上关系。
这是图片处理流程，不属于实时更新要解决的连接或传播问题。
optionExplanations_en: First hop: the protocol between the client and the server holding its connection, e.g. polling vs WebSocket.
Second hop: the update has to travel from its source to the server holding the connection, often via pub/sub or routing.
That's frontend build tooling — it doesn't belong to either hop of the realtime model.
That's image processing, not part of the connection or propagation problem realtime updates actually solve.
scenario: Uber 乘客要看司机实时位置：司机上报落在 A 机器，乘客的连接却挂在 B 机器上。
scenario_en: In Uber, a rider watches the driver's live location, but the driver's update lands on server A while the rider's connection sits on server B.

q: 按正确顺序排列实时消息从产生到客户端显示的两跳路径：
q_en: Put the two-hop path of a realtime message in order.
steps: 连接 server 通过 WebSocket/SSE/long polling 把消息发给客户端
某个事件源产生更新，例如用户发送消息或司机位置变化
更新通过 polling、consistent hash routing 或 pub/sub 到达持有连接的 server
客户端处理消息并更新 UI
why: 实时系统不只是选协议，还要把更新从产生处路由到当前持有用户连接的 server，这是常被忽略的第二跳。
why_en: A realtime update is produced, propagated to the right server, delivered over a client connection, and rendered by the client.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Source[Update Source] --> Prop[Server-side propagation]
  Prop --> Conn[Connection Server]
  Conn --> Client[Client UI]
tradeoff: 低延迟直连交付 vs 多服务器间事件路由的额外开销

q: 标准 HTTP request-response 为什么不适合真正实时的服务器主动推送？
q_en: Why is standard HTTP request-response a poor fit for true server-initiated realtime push?
options: HTTP 流量必须绕开 load balancer，否则请求会被丢弃
HTTP 请求体只能是纯文本，无法携带 JSON 这类结构化数据
客户端请求后服务器响应并关闭连接，服务器没有自然渠道主动发后续事件
HTTP 协议本身只定义了图片传输，不支持其他数据类型
why: 传统 HTTP 是一次性拉取模型，响应后连接关闭；要推送后续事件就得反复拉取，或建立持久连接换服务器主动权。
why_en: Traditional HTTP is request-response, so servers need polling or persistent connections to deliver later events.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server
    C->>S: HTTP request
    S-->>C: response
    Note over C,S: 连接结束
    S--xC: 后续事件无法自然推送
options_en: HTTP traffic must avoid load balancers or requests get dropped.
HTTP request bodies are plain text only and cannot carry structured data like JSON.
The server responds once and closes the connection, leaving no natural channel to push later events.
HTTP as a protocol only defines image transfer, not other data types.
tradeoff: 一次性请求响应 vs 持续开放的推送通道

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是大多数 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP, HyperText Transfer Protocol, is the request-response protocol most web communication is built on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种轻量级的结构化数据格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: JSON is a lightweight structured data format.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把请求分发到多台后端服务器的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer distributes incoming requests across multiple backend servers.

optionExplanations: 不成立：HTTP 流量本来就要经过 load balancer，不存在必须绕开的限制。
站不住脚：HTTP body 能传输 JSON 等任意结构化数据，不限于纯文本。
抓住了根因：响应后连接关闭，服务器没有天然的后续推送渠道，只能反复拉取或换成持久连接。
说错了：HTTP 是通用协议，图片只是它能传输的众多数据类型之一。
optionExplanations_en: Not true: HTTP traffic normally does go through a load balancer; there's no rule requiring it to bypass one.
Doesn't hold up: an HTTP body can carry JSON or any structured payload, not just plain text.
Nails the root cause: once the response returns the connection closes, leaving the server no natural channel to push later events.
Wrong: HTTP is a general-purpose protocol; images are just one of many data types it can carry.
scenario: 股票行情页现在用普通 HTTP GET 拉价格，产品要求价格一变就 200ms 内推到页面。
scenario_en: A stock quote page pulls prices with plain HTTP GET today, but the product now wants any price change pushed to the page within 200 milliseconds.

q: 在面试讨论实时连接时，TCP 相比 UDP 的关键语义是什么？
q_en: In realtime connection interviews, what key semantics does TCP provide compared with UDP?
options: TCP 无法支撑 WebSocket 这类需要双向发送消息的持久连接
TCP 是 connectionless 协议，发送数据不需要事先握手，也不保证到达顺序
TCP 只服务于 DNS 查询这类短请求，不适合承载持续的数据流
TCP 是 connection-oriented，保证有序可靠传输，但连接建立和维护有成本
why: WebSocket、HTTP、SSE 等都建立在 TCP 语义之上。持久连接带来低延迟，也带来服务端连接状态成本。
why_en: TCP provides ordered reliable connections, which help realtime protocols but require connection state.
scenario: 面试官问你为什么 WebSocket、HTTP 这些实时协议都构建在 TCP 而不是 UDP 之上。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks why protocols like WebSocket and HTTP are built on TCP instead of UDP.
options_en: TCP cannot support persistent connections like WebSocket that need bidirectional messaging.
TCP is a connectionless protocol that needs no handshake and does not guarantee arrival order.
TCP only serves short requests like DNS lookups and cannot carry a sustained data stream.
TCP is connection-oriented and guarantees ordered, reliable delivery, but setting up and maintaining the connection has a cost.
tradeoff: 有序可靠但要维护连接状态（TCP） vs 无连接更轻但不保证送达顺序（UDP）

rows: 视频/游戏等能容忍丢包

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、保证有序可靠传输的传输层协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees ordered, reliable delivery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、不保证顺序或送达的传输层协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP, User Datagram Protocol, is a connectionless transport protocol that does not guarantee order or delivery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析成 IP 地址的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS, the Domain Name System, resolves domain names into IP addresses.

optionExplanations: 说反了：TCP 恰恰是 WebSocket 等持久双向连接的基础，不存在无法支撑的问题。
把 UDP 的 connectionless、不保证顺序这些特性错按到了 TCP 头上，两者搞反了。
把 TCP 的适用范围错误缩小成只服务 DNS 这类短请求，与它承载持续数据流的事实不符。
抓住关键：TCP 先握手建连、之后保证有序可靠传输，代价是要维护连接状态。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: TCP is exactly what persistent bidirectional connections like WebSocket rely on.
That description swaps TCP and UDP — connectionless, no ordering guarantee is UDP's behavior, not TCP's.
Wrongly narrows TCP's scope to short DNS-style requests, when it actually carries sustained data streams fine.
The key point: TCP handshakes first, then guarantees ordered reliable delivery, at the cost of maintaining connection state.

q: L4 和 L7 load balancer 对实时连接的关键区别是什么？
q_en: What is the key difference between L4 and L7 load balancers for realtime connections?
options: L4 在 TCP/UDP 层转发，更贴近持久连接；L7 懂 HTTP 但可能重建后端连接
L7 只理解二进制 UDP 报文，L4 只能转发 JSON 格式的应用数据
L4 能读懂 HTTP header 按 URL path 路由，L7 只能看 IP 和端口
L4 和 L7 都必须终止 TCP 连接，所以都无法支撑长连接实时系统
why: L4 更贴近“直连同一台后端”的心智模型，适合 WebSocket 等持久连接；L7 能按内容路由，但可能拆断重建后端连接。
why_en: L4 load balancers are closer to persistent TCP connections, while L7 load balancers provide application routing but can complicate connection semantics.
scenario: 系统要给 WebSocket 这类长连接选负载均衡层，你要比较 L4 和 L7 load balancer 的行为差异。
scenario_en: You need to choose a load-balancing layer for long-lived WebSocket connections and compare L4 and L7 behavior.
options_en: L4 forwards at the TCP/UDP layer, closer to persistent connections; L7 reads HTTP but may rebuild the backend connection.
L7 can only forward raw UDP packets, and L4 can only forward JSON application data.
L4 can read HTTP headers and route by URL path, while L7 only sees IP and port.
Both L4 and L7 must terminate the TCP connection, so neither can support long-lived realtime systems.
tradeoff: L4 贴近持久连接、转发快 vs L7 能按内容路由但可能拆分连接

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 TCP/UDP 层转发流量，不解析应用层内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An L4 load balancer forwards traffic at the TCP/UDP layer without parsing application content.

termDefinitions.meaning: 理解 HTTP 等应用层协议，可按内容路由。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An L7 load balancer understands application-layer protocols like HTTP and can route based on content.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、保证有序可靠传输的传输层协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees ordered, reliable delivery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、不保证顺序或送达的传输层协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP, User Datagram Protocol, is a connectionless transport protocol that does not guarantee order or delivery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是大多数 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP, HyperText Transfer Protocol, is the request-response protocol most web communication is built on.

optionExplanations: 抓住区别：L4 在 TCP/UDP 层直接转发，最贴近持久连接；L7 能读 HTTP 内容，但可能拆断连接再建到后端。
说反了：能解析应用层内容的是 L7，能转发任意二进制数据的是 L4，这里两者角色对调了。
说反了：读 HTTP header 按 path 路由是 L7 的能力，L4 只看 IP 和端口。
不成立：L4 通常不终止应用层连接，直连语义正是它更贴近长连接的原因。
optionExplanations_en: Nails the split: L4 forwards raw TCP/UDP and stays closest to a persistent connection; L7 reads HTTP but may tear down and rebuild the backend leg.
Swapped: parsing application content is L7's job, and forwarding any binary data is L4's — this option reverses them.
Swapped: reading HTTP headers to route by path is what L7 does, while L4 only sees IP and port.
Not true: L4 typically doesn't terminate the application connection, which is exactly why it stays closer to long-lived connections.

scenario: 某功能只需要每 2-5 秒刷新一次状态，低延迟不是核心；你想保留面试时间给更重要的系统部分。
scenario_en: A feature only needs status refreshes every 2 to 5 seconds, low latency is not critical, and you want to save interview time for more important parts.
q: 最务实的起点是什么？
q_en: What is the most pragmatic starting point?
options: WebRTC mesh（客户端两两直连）
Simple polling（客户端定期拉取）
自研一套 TCP 协议
强制所有客户端都建立 WebSocket 长连接
why: 不是所有“更新”都要求真正实时。简单轮询无特殊基础设施、stateless、容易解释，是很好的 baseline。
why_en: If low latency is not critical, simple polling is a pragmatic baseline that avoids realtime infrastructure complexity.
whenOtherWins: 如果消息必须毫秒级送达或频率很高，应升级到 long polling、SSE 或 WebSocket。
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server
    C->>S: poll
    S-->>C: no change
    C->>S: poll later
    S-->>C: new status
options_en: WebRTC mesh — browsers connect directly to each other peer to peer.
Simple polling — the client asks the server on a regular interval.
Build a custom TCP protocol from scratch.
Force every client to hold open a WebSocket connection.
tradeoff: 先用最省心的轮询保住面试时间 vs 提前上重基础设施换低延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: 支持浏览器间直接点对点音视频/数据通信的协议族。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebRTC is a protocol suite that lets browsers exchange audio, video, or data directly, peer to peer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、保证有序可靠传输的传输层协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees ordered, reliable delivery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在一条 TCP 连接上支持客户端和服务器双向收发消息的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol that lets client and server exchange messages both ways over one persistent connection.

optionExplanations: WebRTC mesh 是给点对点音视频设计的，这里只是要拿到状态更新，上它是杀鸡用牛刀。
延迟要求宽松、想省面试时间时最务实：无需特殊基础设施，客户端定期拉取就够。
自研传输层协议要重新解决可靠性和顺序问题，这里的低频需求完全用不上这个投入。
低延迟不是核心诉求时，强制所有人维持长连接只是白白多背状态管理成本。
optionExplanations_en: WebRTC mesh is built for peer-to-peer audio/video, overkill just to fetch a status update here.
The pragmatic call when latency is loose and you want to save interview time: no special infra, the client just polls on an interval.
Rolling your own transport protocol means re-solving reliability and ordering — way more investment than this low-frequency need justifies.
When low latency isn't the core ask, forcing everyone onto a persistent connection just adds state-management cost for nothing.

q: Simple polling 的优缺点有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are the pros and cons of simple polling? (Select all that apply.)
options: 实现简单、stateless、兼容所有 HTTP 基础设施
延迟最高，最多延迟一个 polling interval 加请求处理时间
更新不频繁但客户端很多时会造成大量空读
天然支持全双工低延迟通信
why: 轮询的简单性很有价值，但代价是延迟和无效请求。它不是 full-duplex 实时通道。
why_en: Simple polling is easy and stateless but adds latency and wasted reads when updates are infrequent.
options_en: Simple to implement, stateless, and compatible with any standard HTTP infrastructure.
Latency is the highest, up to one polling interval plus request handling time.
Infrequent updates with many clients create a lot of wasted empty reads.
It naturally supports full-duplex low-latency communication.
tradeoff: 响应更新的简单性 vs 延迟与浪费请求

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器不为单个客户端保留连接状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stateless means the server keeps no per-client connection state between requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 双方可以同时发送和接收数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Full-duplex means both sides can send and receive at the same time.

optionExplanations: 实现代价最低：无状态、走标准 HTTP，任何网关和负载均衡都能直接支持。
代价：更新最多要等一个 polling interval 加处理时间才被看到，是几种方案里延迟最高的。
代价：客户端多、更新稀疏时，大部分轮询请求都是白跑一趟，浪费资源。
不成立：轮询是单向拉取，不具备全双工能力，这条描述的是 WebSocket。
optionExplanations_en: Cheapest to build: stateless and rides on standard HTTP, so any gateway or load balancer already supports it.
The cost: an update can wait up to one polling interval plus processing time before it's seen — the highest latency option here.
The cost: with many clients and infrequent updates, most polls come back empty and waste resources.
Not true: polling is one-way pull, not full-duplex — that description fits WebSocket, not polling.
scenario: 内部工单看板：200 个客服盯着状态，工单一天只变几十次，团队没人做连接层运维。
scenario_en: An internal ticket dashboard: 200 agents watch statuses, tickets change only a few dozen times a day, and nobody on the team can operate a connection tier.

q: 这个量级最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design judgment does this scale estimate most support?
options: 轮询产生的读压力可能被低估，需要专门评估数据库/网关能否扛住
轮询天然比 WebSocket 省资源，不用考虑扩容
10 万 QPS 对任何数据库都无压力，无需缓存或限流
客户端越多轮询请求会自然错峰分散，读压力被自动摊平不用额外评估
why: 公式：100 万 ÷ 10 秒 = 10 万 QPS（每秒查询数）；轮询的简单性掩盖了真实读压力，这个数字决定要不要给网关/DB 加限流或缓存。
why_en: One million clients polling every ten seconds is about one hundred thousand queries per second, so polling's simplicity can hide a real read-load problem that capacity planning must account for.
scenario: 系统用 simple polling，100 万客户端每 10 秒轮询一次；换算下来后端要扛约 10 万 QPS 的读请求。
scenario_en: The system uses simple polling: one million clients poll every ten seconds, which works out to roughly one hundred thousand read requests per second.
options_en: The read load from polling can be underestimated, so you must check whether the database or gateway can absorb it.
Polling is naturally cheaper than WebSocket, so no extra capacity planning is needed.
One hundred thousand QPS is trivial for any database, so no caching or throttling is needed.
With more clients the polls naturally spread across seconds, so the read load evens out on its own with no extra review.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒钟处理的查询次数，用来衡量读压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS, or Queries Per Second, measures how many read requests a system handles every second.

optionExplanations: 抓住数字的设计含义：10 万 QPS 是真实读压力，得专门评估网关和数据库能不能扛住，不能想当然。
不成立：轮询同样要处理这 10 万 QPS 的读请求，资源开销不会因为不是 WebSocket 就自动省下来。
低估了风险：10 万 QPS 对多数数据库其实是不小的压力，跳过缓存/限流评估很危险。
不成立：轮询请求不会自动错峰，客户端增多只会叠加读压力，仍要专门评估网关和 DB。
optionExplanations_en: Captures the design implication: 100k QPS is real read load, so you must explicitly check whether the gateway and database can absorb it.
Not true: polling still has to serve that same 100k QPS of reads; skipping WebSocket doesn't make the resource cost disappear.
Underestimates the risk: 100k QPS is a real load for most databases, and skipping the caching/throttling review is dangerous.
Not true: polls don't automatically spread out; more clients just stack up read pressure, which still needs an explicit gateway/DB review.

q: HTTP keep-alive 如何降低 simple polling 的开销？
q_en: How does HTTP keep-alive reduce simple polling overhead?
options: 让每一次轮询请求都自动跳过数据库读取，并直接从边缘缓存里返回命中的已有结果
让服务器绕开 HTTP 直接给客户端推送无限条消息
把 polling interval 自动缩短到 0 让请求变成实时
让多次 polling 复用 TCP 连接，减少重复握手和 teardown
why: 如果 keep-alive 比 polling interval 长，多次请求能复用同一条 TCP 连接，省掉重复握手和 teardown 的开销。

options: 这条连接只能用来单向下载图片文件，无法传输文本或其他任意类型的数据
只支持服务器往客户端单向推送文本内容，不能反向发送消息
一条持久连接上，client 和 server 都能双向发消息
每发送一条消息都要重新建立一次全新的 HTTP 连接
why: WebSocket 是 full-duplex 通道，适合聊天、协作编辑、游戏等高频双向通信。
why_en: WebSocket provides full-duplex communication over a persistent connection.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    C["Client"] <-->|WebSocket| W["WS Server"]
    W --> B["Backend"]
    B --> W
    W --> C
options_en: This connection can only download image files one-way and cannot carry text or any other kind of data.
It only supports a one-way text push from server to client, never the other way.
Over one persistent connection, both client and server can send messages both ways.
Every single message requires establishing a brand-new HTTP connection from scratch.

Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade

# 此后同一条 TCP 连接上双向收发消息帧

termDefinitions.meaning: 双方可以同时发送和接收数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Full-duplex means both sides can send and receive at the same time.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 请求头，用来把连接从 HTTP 协议切换到另一个协议如 WebSocket。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Upgrade header asks HTTP to switch the connection to another protocol such as WebSocket.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在一条 TCP 连接上支持客户端和服务器双向收发消息的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol that lets client and server exchange messages both ways over one persistent connection.

optionExplanations: 不成立：WebSocket 能传任意二进制或文本数据，不限于图片下载。
说错了协议：单向文本推送是 SSE 的行为，WebSocket 的关键正是能双向发。
抓住关键能力：一条持久连接上，client 和 server 都能随时主动发消息。
不成立：这恰恰是它要解决的问题——建好一次连接后不用每条消息都重新握手。
optionExplanations_en: Not true: WebSocket can carry any binary or text data, not just image downloads.
Wrong protocol: one-way text push describes SSE — WebSocket's whole point is that both sides can send.
The key capability: over one persistent connection, both client and server can send messages at any time.
Not true: avoiding a fresh handshake per message is exactly the problem WebSocket solves.
scenario: 协作白板上每个人的笔画要毫秒级同步给其他人，客户端也在不停往上发操作。
scenario_en: On a collaborative whiteboard, everyone's strokes must sync to others within milliseconds while clients keep sending operations upward.

q: 按正确顺序排列 WebSocket 建连流程：
q_en: Put the WebSocket connection setup flow in order.
steps: 连接升级为 WebSocket protocol
连接保持打开，双方发送消息
客户端发起 HTTP/WebSocket handshake
连接显式关闭或断线后需要重连
why: WebSocket 借助 HTTP upgrade 建立，之后不再是普通 request-response 模型。
why_en: WebSocket starts with an HTTP upgrade handshake, then keeps a bidirectional message connection open.

termDefinitions.meaning: 建立连接前，双方交换信息确认协议和参数的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A handshake is the initial exchange that establishes a connection and agrees on protocol parameters.

scenario: 聊天应用中，用户既要实时收消息，也要频繁发消息、typing indicators 和 presence updates。
scenario_en: In a chat app, users need to receive messages in realtime and frequently send messages, typing indicators, and presence updates.
q: 客户端连接协议最适合什么？
q_en: Which client connection protocol fits best?
options: 用 S3 presigned URL 直传消息文件
每日批处理消息
只用简单轮询查新消息
WebSocket 双向长连接
why: 聊天是典型高频双向通信。WebSocket 降低每条消息的 HTTP overhead，也支持 server push 和 client writes。
why_en: Chat is a classic high-frequency bidirectional use case for WebSockets.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是偶尔发写请求、主要接收服务器推送，SSE + HTTP POST 可能更简单。
options_en: Use S3 presigned URLs to upload message files directly.
Batch-process messages once a day.
Use only simple polling to check for new messages.
A bidirectional persistent WebSocket connection.
tradeoff: 高频双向消息的实时性 vs 持久连接的状态管理成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 在一条 TCP 连接上支持客户端和服务器双向收发消息的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol that lets client and server exchange messages both ways over one persistent connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带临时签名的 URL，让客户端能直接读写对象存储而不经过后端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A presigned URL is a temporary signed link that lets a client read or write object storage directly.

optionExplanations: presigned URL 是给客户端直传对象存储用的，管的是文件上传，不是消息收发通道。
每日批处理的延迟以天计，聊天需要的是秒级甚至毫秒级的即时送达。
轮询对高频双向的聊天来说延迟高、请求量大，发消息和收消息都不顺畅。
收发都很频繁时的直接选择：一条持久连接上双向低开销地传消息。
optionExplanations_en: A presigned URL is for uploading files straight to object storage — that's file transfer, not a messaging channel.
Daily batching means day-scale delay; chat needs delivery within seconds, not once a day.
Polling adds high latency and request volume for something this bidirectional and frequent — both sending and receiving suffer.
The direct fit when both sides send and receive often: one persistent connection carries messages both ways cheaply.

q: WebSocket 的典型复杂度包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: What typical complexities come with WebSocket? (Select all that apply.)
options: 状态连接增加 load balancing 和扩缩容复杂度
部署时要处理旧连接断开和重连
断线期间可能漏消息，需要补发机制
它完全不需要特殊基础设施支持
why: WebSocket 的性能收益来自持久连接，但持久连接也是状态。生产系统要专门处理连接生命周期。
why_en: WebSockets add stateful connection management, deployment, reconnection, and missed-message concerns.
options_en: Stateful connections add complexity to load balancing and scaling.
Deployments must handle disconnecting old connections and reconnecting clients.
Messages can be missed during a disconnect and need a replay mechanism.
It needs no special infrastructure support at all.
tradeoff: 持久连接带来的性能收益 vs 状态管理和部署复杂度
optionExplanations: 代价：连接是有状态的，负载均衡和扩缩容都得考虑“粘在哪台机器上”。
代价：每次部署重启都要优雅断开旧连接，并让客户端重连到新实例。
代价：断线那段时间的消息可能漏掉，得靠日志或队列补发才能补齐。
不成立：WebSocket 恰恰需要专门的连接层基础设施来管理这些长连接。
optionExplanations_en: The cost: connections are stateful, so load balancing and scaling both have to account for which server a client is stuck on.
The cost: every deploy has to gracefully drop old connections and get clients reconnected to new instances.
The cost: messages sent during a disconnect can be missed, and only a log or queue can replay them.
Not true: WebSocket specifically needs dedicated connection-layer infrastructure to manage all those long-lived connections.
scenario: 聊天服务用 WebSocket 扛 100 万条长连接，同时每周要滚动发布两次新版本。
scenario_en: A chat service carries a million WebSocket connections while shipping a rolling deploy twice a week.

scenario: 你不想让整个后端都背负 WebSocket statefulness，只想把连接管理集中在少数服务里。
scenario_en: You do not want the whole backend to carry WebSocket state, so you want connection management isolated in a small set of services.
q: 常见架构选择是什么？
q_en: What is the common architecture choice?
options: 终止到专门 WebSocket service，后端保持 stateless
让系统里每一个微服务都各自独立地直接维护自己面向客户端的长连接和连接状态
把原本应该在服务端保存的连接状态直接放进前端浏览器代码里
禁止系统里所有用户重新连接，断线之后必须重新登录整个系统
why: 专门连接层负责连接、重连、fanout 和轻量转发，其他服务通过 pub/sub 或 RPC 与它交互。
why_en: A dedicated WebSocket service contains connection state so the rest of the backend can stay stateless.
whenOtherWins: 小系统可以先让应用服务直接持有连接；规模上来后再拆专门连接层。

options_en: Terminate connections in a dedicated WebSocket service, keeping the backend stateless.
Have every single microservice independently and separately maintain its own client-facing long-lived connections and connection state.
Take the connection state that should live on the server and put it directly inside the frontend browser code.
Forbid every user in the system from reconnecting; force a full re-login after any disconnect.
tradeoff: 把状态收敛到一个专门服务 vs 让状态散布到所有业务服务里

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器不为单个客户端保留连接状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stateless means the server keeps no per-client connection state between requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在一条 TCP 连接上支持客户端和服务器双向收发消息的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol that lets client and server exchange messages both ways over one persistent connection.

optionExplanations: 把状态收敛到一处：专门的 WebSocket service 在入口终止连接，其余业务服务保持无状态。
不成立：让每个微服务都各自维护连接，状态到处扩散，正是想避免的局面。
不成立：连接状态本来就是服务端维持的，放进前端代码里刷新一下就丢了。
不成立：禁止重连只会毁掉体验，也没有解决状态该放在哪里这个问题。
optionExplanations_en: Contains the state in one place: a dedicated WebSocket service terminates connections at the edge, keeping the rest of the backend stateless.
Not true: having every microservice maintain its own connections spreads state everywhere — exactly what this is trying to avoid.
Not true: connection state has to live on the server; putting it in frontend code means a page refresh wipes it out.
Not true: banning reconnects just wrecks the user experience without answering where the state should actually live.

q: WebRTC 最适合什么场景？
q_en: What use case is WebRTC best suited for?
options: 只是偶尔刷新一次的 dashboard 数字展示界面
浏览器间直接音视频、屏幕共享或高频 P2P 通信
每隔 10 秒查一次状态，属于延迟不敏感的场景
数据库把一整批写入合并成一次事务来提交
why: WebRTC 是最复杂选项，适合需要 P2P 降低延迟/服务器带宽的场景。普通实时通知通常用 SSE/WebSocket。
why_en: WebRTC fits peer-to-peer audio, video, screen sharing, gaming, or high-frequency collaboration.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["Browser A"] <-->|P2P 媒体/数据| B["Browser B"]
    A -.信令.-> S["Server"]
    B -.信令.-> S
options_en: Just a dashboard interface that refreshes a number infrequently.
Direct browser-to-browser audio/video, screen sharing, or high-frequency P2P.
Checking status every ten seconds, a case where latency doesn't matter.
A database committing a whole batch of writes as one single transaction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 支持浏览器间直接点对点音视频/数据通信的协议族。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebRTC is a protocol suite that lets browsers exchange audio, video, or data directly, peer to peer.

scenario: 候选方案要选一个协议来支撑浏览器间的高清音视频通话、屏幕共享和文档协作场景。
scenario_en: You are choosing a protocol for browser-to-browser HD video calls, screen sharing, and document collaboration.
optionExplanations: 这类低频场景 simple polling 就够，不需要 WebRTC 的建连复杂度。
抓住定位：浏览器间直接点对点传音视频、屏幕共享或高频数据，是 WebRTC 的强项。
10 秒一次的低频查询延迟不敏感，用不上 P2P 直连带来的复杂度。
数据库事务提交是存储层内部机制，和浏览器间的 P2P 通信完全是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: This kind of infrequent refresh is fine with simple polling — no need for WebRTC's connection-setup complexity.
The actual fit: direct peer-to-peer audio/video, screen sharing, or high-frequency data between browsers is exactly WebRTC's strength.
Checking every 10 seconds is latency-insensitive, so there's no reason to take on P2P's connection complexity.
A database transaction commit is an internal storage mechanism, unrelated to peer-to-peer communication between browsers.

q: WebRTC 建连通常涉及哪些组件或概念？（多选）
q_en: Which components or concepts are usually involved in WebRTC setup? (Select all that apply.)
options: Signaling server 交换连接信息
ICE candidates
STUN 用于 NAT traversal
TURN relay 在直连失败时转发流量
why: WebRTC 的复杂度主要来自 NAT/firewall 和连接协商。Signaling 本身也需要某种实时通道。
why_en: WebRTC setup involves signaling, ICE candidates, STUN, and often TURN relays.
options_en: A signaling server exchanges connection info between peers.
ICE candidates.
STUN discovers a routable address for NAT traversal.
A TURN relay forwards traffic when a direct connection fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 帮助两个 peer 交换连接信息的服务器，不承担媒体流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A signaling server helps two peers exchange connection info; it does not carry the media traffic itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 收集和交换候选连接地址、尝试建立可用路径的框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ICE, Interactive Connectivity Establishment, is the framework that gathers and tries candidate addresses to find a working path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 帮助 peer 发现自己的公网可路由地址，用于 NAT 穿透。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: STUN, Session Traversal Utilities for NAT, helps a peer discover its own publicly routable address for NAT traversal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 直连失败时作为中继服务器转发全部流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TURN, Traversal Using Relays around NAT, relays all traffic through a server when a direct connection fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让多台内网设备共用一个公网地址的机制，常阻碍 P2P 直连。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NAT, Network Address Translation, lets many private devices share one public address, which often blocks direct P2P connections.

optionExplanations: signaling server 负责在建连前帮双方交换 offer/answer 等连接信息，它本身不转发媒体流量。
ICE candidate 是每个 peer 能被外部访问到的地址候选集合，双方靠它们尝试匹配出可用路径。
STUN 帮 peer 发现自己的公网可路由地址，用来穿透 NAT、尝试直连。
直连失败时，TURN 作为中继服务器转发全部流量，兜底可靠性但更耗带宽。
optionExplanations_en: A signaling server helps the two peers exchange offer/answer connection info before the link is set up; it never carries the media itself.
ICE candidates are the set of addresses each peer might be reachable at, and both sides try pairing them to find a working path.
STUN helps a peer discover its own public, routable address so it can punch through NAT and attempt a direct connection.
When a direct connection fails, TURN relays all the traffic through a server — a reliable fallback at the cost of bandwidth.
scenario: 做 1v1 视频通话，两端都在家用路由器 NAT 后面，你希望媒体流尽量不经过自己的服务器。
scenario_en: You're building one-on-one video calls where both peers sit behind home-router NAT, and you want media to avoid your own servers when possible.

q: STUN 和 TURN 的区别是什么？
q_en: What is the difference between STUN and TURN?
options: TURN 只是一种用于 SQL 事务提交的服务，和媒体流传输毫无关系
STUN 其实是一种数据库，TURN 其实是一种 CDN 服务
STUN 帮助发现可路由地址/打洞；TURN 作为中继服务器转发流量
STUN 和 TURN 都只是 SSE 协议里的可选参数
why: STUN 尝试促成 P2P 直连；TURN 是直连失败时的 relay，成本和延迟更高但可靠性更好。
why_en: STUN helps peers discover routable paths, while TURN relays traffic when direct peer connections fail.
options_en: TURN is just a service for SQL transaction commits, with nothing to do with media traffic.
STUN is actually a database, and TURN is actually a CDN.
STUN helps discover a routable address for hole punching; TURN relays traffic as a fallback server.
Both STUN and TURN are just optional parameters of SSE.
tradeoff: STUN 优先促成直连、省服务器带宽 vs TURN 兜底可靠但要转发全部流量

rows: 尝试后走 P2P 直连

termDefinitions.meaningEn: STUN, Session Traversal Utilities for NAT, helps a peer discover its own publicly routable address for NAT traversal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 直连失败时作为中继服务器转发全部流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TURN, Traversal Using Relays around NAT, relays all traffic through a server when a direct connection fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让多台内网设备共用一个公网地址的机制，常阻碍 P2P 直连。

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 HTTP 的单向流：服务器持续推送事件，客户端只接收。

optionExplanations: 不成立：TURN 和 SQL 事务毫无关系，它转发的是 WebRTC 建连失败后的媒体流量。
不成立：两者都不是存储或分发产品，STUN 和 TURN 都是 NAT 穿透相关的网络服务。
抓住区别：STUN 帮忙发现可路由地址、尝试打洞直连；TURN 在直连失败时充当中继转发。
不成立：STUN/TURN 是 WebRTC 建连用的独立协议，和 SSE 没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Not true: TURN has nothing to do with SQL transactions — it relays WebRTC media traffic after a direct connection fails.
Not true: neither is a storage or distribution product — both STUN and TURN are networking services for NAT traversal.
The actual split: STUN helps discover a routable address and attempt a direct hole-punched connection; TURN relays traffic as a fallback when that fails.
Not true: STUN and TURN are standalone protocols used in WebRTC connection setup, unrelated to SSE.
scenario: 视频通话上线后约 15% 用户在企业防火墙后打洞失败，但这些通话仍然必须能接通。
scenario_en: After launch, about 15 percent of video-call users sit behind corporate firewalls where hole punching fails, yet those calls still have to connect.

scenario: live dashboard 只需要服务器不断推送指标，用户很少向服务器发送消息。
scenario_en: A live dashboard only needs the server to keep pushing metrics, and users rarely send messages back.
q: 协议选择上更偏向什么？
q_en: Which protocol choice is the better fit?
options: 自己在 UDP 上从零实现推送协议
WebRTC 建 P2P 通道传指标
认为双向 WebSocket 是唯一选择
SSE 单向推送指标
why: 单向 server-to-client 更新是 SSE 的强项。它比 WebSocket 少很多状态和双向通信复杂度。
why_en: SSE is a good fit for one-way server-to-client dashboard updates.
whenOtherWins: 如果 dashboard 还需要高频双向控制命令，WebSocket 可以更合适。
options_en: Build a custom push protocol from scratch on top of UDP.
WebRTC opens a peer-to-peer channel to carry metrics.
Assume bidirectional WebSocket is the only option.
SSE pushes metrics one way to the client.
tradeoff: 单向推送够用就选轻量方案 vs 上双向/自研方案的额外复杂度

termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, Server-Sent Events, is an HTTP-based one-way stream where the server keeps pushing events to the client.

termDefinitions.meaning: 支持浏览器间直接点对点音视频/数据通信的协议族。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebRTC is a protocol suite that lets browsers exchange audio, video, or data directly, peer to peer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在一条 TCP 连接上支持客户端和服务器双向收发消息的协议。

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、不保证顺序或送达的传输层协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP, User Datagram Protocol, is a connectionless transport protocol that does not guarantee order or delivery.

optionExplanations: 在 UDP 上从零实现可靠推送要重新造轮子解决顺序和丢包问题，成本远超这个场景需要。
P2P 通道是给客户端互连设计的，这里只是服务器往外推指标，用不上它的直连能力。
双向能力这里根本用不上：用户很少发消息，只是单纯需要看服务器推送。
服务器只需要单向推送，SSE 比 WebSocket 少了状态和双向管理的复杂度，刚好够用。
optionExplanations_en: Rolling a push protocol on raw UDP means re-solving ordering and packet loss yourself — way more cost than this needs.
A P2P channel is for connecting clients to each other; here it's just the server pushing metrics, so direct-connect capability goes unused.
Bidirectional isn't needed here at all — users rarely send anything, they just need to receive server pushes.
The server only needs to push one way, and SSE gets that done with less state and complexity than WebSocket requires.

scenario: 在线多人游戏需要最低延迟、双向频繁状态交换，部分通信可 P2P。
scenario_en: An online multiplayer game needs very low latency and frequent bidirectional state exchange, with some communication allowed to be peer to peer.
q: 可能考虑哪种协议？
q_en: Which protocol might you consider?
options: WebRTC 或 WebSocket，取决于是否需要 P2P
把游戏状态做成每日 batch export
只用 30 秒一次的 simple polling 同步状态
靠 S3 lifecycle rule 管理游戏存档
why: 互动游戏要求高频低延迟双向通信。WebSocket 适合 server-coordinated，WebRTC 适合 P2P 降低延迟和服务器带宽。

q: 使用 WebSocket/SSE 这类持久连接后，发送给某个用户的更新为什么需要路由？
q_en: Why do updates need routing after you use persistent connections like WebSocket or SSE?

因为用户连接只存在某台 server 内存中，更新源必须找到或广播到那台 server
why: 连接本身是 server-side state。要么让用户稳定连接到可预测 server，要么用 pub/sub 让 endpoint server 订阅相关 topic。
why_en: Persistent connections create server-side state, so updates must reach the server holding that user's connection.
options_en: Because HTTP's request-message format is fundamentally unable to carry a business identifier field like a user ID.
Because the client's network device and carrier link fundamentally cannot receive any server-pushed message.
Because every persistent connection's full state is actually auto-persisted into a backend relational database.
Because that user's connection lives only in one server's memory, the update source must find or broadcast to that server.

q: 用 consistent hashing 做实时连接路由的基本想法是什么？
q_en: What is the basic idea behind using consistent hashing for realtime connection routing?
options: 把用户/文档和 server 映射到 hash ring，归属可预测
把所有客户端发来的消息不做任何区分地统一写进同一个 Redis key 排队
让客户端每一次建立连接都随机挑选一台 server，并且从不做任何重定向处理
用 CDN 边缘节点去缓存住 WebSocket 长连接上产生的所有消息内容

why_en: Consistent hashing assigns each user or entity to a predictable connection server while minimizing movement during scaling.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    K["user/doc id"] --> H["hash"]
    H --> R(("ring"))
    R --> S["owner server"]
    S --> C["该 key 的连接"]

Write every client's messages, without distinction, into the same single Redis key to queue up.
Let clients pick a random server on every single connection and never redirect them at all.

Not true: picking a random server with no redirect means the update source can never find where the user's connection actually lives.
Not true: CDN edge caching is for reusable static content — it can't cache a stateful long-lived connection.

q: server-side propagation 更可能考虑什么？

q: Consistent hashing 扩缩容时应讨论哪些机制？（多选）
q_en: What mechanisms should you discuss when scaling consistent-hashing connection servers? (Select all that apply.)
options: 标记 scaling event，记录旧/新 server assignment
慢慢断开部分客户端，让它们重连到新 owner
过渡期消息同时发往旧 owner 和新 owner
直接让所有连接瞬间断开且不补发消息
why: 扩缩容不只是 hash 算法，还要连接迁移编排。过渡期要避免消息丢失。
why_en: Scaling consistent-hash connection servers needs coordinated migration, reconnects, and duplicate routing during transition.
options_en: Mark the start of a scaling event and record both old and new server assignments.
Slowly disconnect some clients so they reconnect to their new owner.
During the transition, send messages to both the old and new owner.
Disconnect all connections instantly with no replay of missed messages.
optionExplanations: 起点：先标记 scaling event、记录旧/新 assignment，后续迁移才有依据可查。
手段：慢慢断开部分客户端，让它们逐步重连到新 owner，避免瞬时冲击。
手段：过渡期把消息同时发往旧/新 owner，防止迁移窗口期消息找不到人收。

A technique: disconnect clients gradually so they reconnect to the new owner over time instead of all at once.
A technique: during the transition, send messages to both the old and new owner so nothing goes unheard mid-migration.
The failure case: dropping every connection instantly with no replay just loses whatever was in flight during migration.

options: 每个客户端都绕开后端服务，直接对所有数据库实例发起查询
不管更新源是谁，客户端都必须每一次连接同一台固定不变的 server
更新发布到 topic，endpoint servers 订阅并转发给自己的客户端
所有消息都必须先经过同一个中央 API handler 完整同步处理完之后才能返回
why: Pub/Sub 把主要状态放在 pub/sub 层，endpoint server 更轻量，客户端可连任意 endpoint。
why_en: Pub/sub sends updates to topics, and endpoint servers subscribe and forward them to connected clients.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    P["Publisher"] --> T["Topic"]
    T --> S1["Endpoint A"]
    T --> S2["Endpoint B"]
    S1 --> C1["Clients"]
    S2 --> C2["Clients"]
options_en: Every client bypasses the backend service and queries all database instances directly.
Regardless of the update source, clients must always connect to the exact same fixed server every time.
Updates publish to a topic, and endpoint servers subscribe and forward them to their own clients.
Every message must first pass fully and synchronously through the same central API handler before it can return.
codeSample:
SUBSCRIBE user:42
PUBLISH user:42 {"type":"message","text":"hi"}
# endpoint server 为每个已连接用户订阅一个 topic
# 更新源只管 PUBLISH，不需要知道用户连接在哪台 server

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布者把消息发到 topic，订阅该 topic 的所有客户端都会收到。

termDefinitions.meaning: pub/sub 里消息分类的频道，订阅者按 topic 接收消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A topic is a named channel in pub/sub that subscribers listen to for messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只负责持有客户端连接、订阅 topic 并转发消息的轻量服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An endpoint server is a lightweight server that just holds client connections, subscribes to topics, and forwards messages.

optionExplanations: 不成立：客户端不会绕开后端直连数据库，那和 Pub/Sub 的转发模型完全是两回事。
不成立：Pub/Sub 恰恰是为了让客户端可以连任意 endpoint server，不用固定绑死一台。
抓住模型：更新发布到 topic 后，负责该用户连接的 server 订阅该 topic，再转发给自己连着的客户端。
不成立：Pub/Sub 是异步转发，不需要所有消息都挤在同一个 handler 里同步处理。
optionExplanations_en: Not true: clients don't bypass the backend to query databases directly — that has nothing to do with how pub/sub forwards messages.
Not true: pub/sub exists precisely so clients can connect to any endpoint server, without being pinned to one fixed machine.
The actual model: once an update publishes to a topic, whichever server holds that user's connection subscribes and forwards it to its own connected clients.
Not true: pub/sub delivery is asynchronous — it doesn't funnel every message through one synchronous handler.
scenario: 聊天 endpoint server 无状态、客户端随机连一台，发布者根本不知道对方连在哪台上。
scenario_en: Chat endpoint servers are stateless and clients connect to a random one, so a publisher has no idea which server the recipient is on.

q: 按正确顺序排列 pub/sub 实时推送流程：
q_en: Put the pub/sub realtime push flow in order.
steps: Update source publish 到相关 topic
客户端连接任意 endpoint server
Endpoint server 收到 topic 消息后查本机 connection map 并转发
Endpoint server 为该用户/房间订阅相关 topic
why: Pub/Sub 让连接归属和消息发布解耦，endpoint server 不需要是某个用户的固定 owner。
why_en: In pub/sub delivery, endpoints subscribe for their connected clients, updates publish to topics, and endpoints forward messages.
tradeoff: 端点服务器可互换、随便连 vs consistent hashing 的稳定归属

scenario: 聊天系统只需要把小消息转发给在线用户，endpoint server 本身没有重状态，负载希望用 least connections 简单均衡。
scenario_en: A chat system only needs to forward small messages to online users; endpoint servers are lightweight, and load should be balanced with least connections.
q: server-side propagation 更适合什么？
q_en: What server-side propagation approach fits better?
options: 只靠 SQL polling 查有没有新消息
对每个用户做 consistent hashing 固定到一台 server
用 WebRTC mesh 让所有人两两互连
Pub/Sub 转发小消息
why: 小消息转发不需要重 owner state。Pub/Sub 简化连接层，让 endpoint servers 轻量可替换。
why_en: Pub/sub fits lightweight message forwarding where endpoint servers do not hold heavy per-user state.
whenOtherWins: 如果连接状态非常重、迁移昂贵，consistent hashing 可能更合适。
options_en: Rely only on SQL polling for new messages.
Pin every user to one fixed server with consistent hashing.
Use a WebRTC mesh so everyone connects directly to everyone.
Pub/sub forwards lightweight messages.
tradeoff: endpoint server 轻量可互换 vs owner server 稳定但要迁移编排

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布者把消息发到 topic，订阅该 topic 的所有客户端都会收到。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/sub, short for publish/subscribe, lets a publisher send to a topic that every subscriber of that topic receives.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种把 key 分配给 server 的算法，扩缩容时只需迁移少量 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing is an algorithm for assigning keys to servers that only moves a small fraction of keys when the server set changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 支持浏览器间直接点对点音视频/数据通信的协议族。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebRTC is a protocol suite that lets browsers exchange audio, video, or data directly, peer to peer.

optionExplanations: SQL polling 对高频双向的聊天消息来说延迟太高，体验上完全不像实时。
固定归属是给重状态连接省的成本，这里消息轻量，用不上这份复杂度。
mesh 连接数按人数平方增长，聊天室人一多连接数就爆炸。
消息轻量、endpoint server 无重状态时的直接选择：topic 只管转发，谁连在哪台机器都不关心。
optionExplanations_en: SQL polling adds too much latency for chat's frequent, bidirectional messages — it just doesn't feel realtime.
Pinned ownership pays off when connections carry heavy state; here messages are lightweight, so that complexity buys nothing.
Mesh connections grow quadratically with headcount — a busy chat room blows up the connection count.
The direct fit when messages are lightweight and endpoints hold no heavy state: topics just forward, with no care for who's connected where.

q: Pub/Sub 模型的优缺点有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are the pros and cons of the Pub/Sub model? (Select all that apply.)
options: endpoint servers 容易用 least-connections 负载均衡
适合广播到大量订阅者
pub/sub service 可能成为瓶颈或单点，需要集群/分片
完全不增加延迟或依赖
why: Pub/Sub 简化 endpoint 层，但把状态和压力集中到 pub/sub 层。Redis cluster、Kafka 等需要按 topic/key 扩展。
why_en: Pub/sub simplifies endpoint servers but can make the pub/sub service a bottleneck or critical dependency.
options_en: Endpoint servers are easy to load-balance with a least-connections strategy.
It efficiently broadcasts updates to a large number of subscribers.
The pub/sub service can become a bottleneck or single point of failure, needing a cluster or sharding.
It adds absolutely no latency or dependency at all.
tradeoff: endpoint 层易扩展 vs pub/sub 服务本身的单点/瓶颈风险

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布者把消息发到 topic，订阅该 topic 的所有客户端都会收到。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/sub, short for publish/subscribe, lets a publisher send to a topic that every subscriber of that topic receives.

optionExplanations: 优势：endpoint server 本身无状态可互换，用 least-connections 均衡起来很直接。
优势：一次发布就能高效广播给同一 topic 下的所有订阅者。
代价：状态和压力都集中到了 pub/sub 层，它本身可能成瓶颈或单点，得靠集群/分片扛住。
不成立：多一层间接转发必然带来一点延迟和一个新的依赖，不可能完全为零。
optionExplanations_en: A plus: endpoint servers are stateless and interchangeable, so least-connections load balancing works cleanly.
A plus: one publish efficiently broadcasts to every subscriber on that topic.
The cost: state and pressure both concentrate in the pub/sub layer, which can itself become a bottleneck or single point of failure without clustering or sharding.
Not true: adding an indirection layer always adds some latency and a new dependency — it can't be exactly zero.
scenario: 聊天系统靠 Redis pub/sub 转发消息，日活涨到 500 万后所有消息都压在这一层。
scenario_en: A chat system forwards every message through Redis pub/sub, and once daily actives reach five million all of that load lands on one layer.

q: 这个额外延迟量级更支持哪条判断？
q_en: What design judgment does this added-latency order of magnitude support?
options: 多出来的延迟通常是个位数毫秒，远低于用户能感知的门槛
Pub/Sub 会让端到端延迟直接增加好几分钟，几乎完全不能用于任何实时场景
Pub/Sub 延迟接近 1 小时，只适合离线批处理
Pub/Sub 服务必然让系统完全不可用
why: 同区的 Redis Pub/Sub 只是多一两跳内存转发，增加的延迟通常是个位数毫秒；真正要关心的是它的可用性（Redis Pub/Sub 不持久化，订阅者断开会丢消息）和分片扩展。托管的云 Pub/Sub 服务延迟更高，要按其文档另算。
why_en: In-region Redis Pub/Sub adds one or two in-memory hops, usually single-digit milliseconds; the real concerns are availability (Redis Pub/Sub does not persist, so disconnected subscribers miss messages) and sharding. Managed cloud pub/sub services have higher latency and must be estimated from their own docs.
scenario: 聊天消息要经过同机房的 Redis Pub/Sub 再转发到持有用户连接的服务器；团队担心这一层间接转发会让实时性变差。同区网络一跳通常是亚毫秒到几毫秒。
scenario_en: Chat messages pass through an in-region Redis Pub/Sub layer before reaching the server holding the user's connection, and the team worries this indirection hurts realtime behavior. One same-region network hop is typically sub-millisecond to a few milliseconds.
options_en: The added latency is usually single-digit milliseconds, far below what users can perceive.
Pub/sub adds several minutes of end-to-end delay, making it nearly unusable for any realtime scenario.
Pub/sub latency is close to an hour, fit only for offline batch.
A pub/sub service inevitably makes the system completely unavailable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布者把消息发到 topic，订阅该 topic 的所有客户端都会收到。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/sub, short for publish/subscribe, lets a publisher send to a topic that every subscriber of that topic receives.

optionExplanations: 抓住量级：这一跳转发通常只有个位数毫秒，远低于用户能感知的门槛，不是需要担心的点。
夸大了：分钟级延迟远超 Pub/Sub 实际增加的开销，这个量级不成立。
夸大了：小时级延迟是批处理系统的量级，这里只是多经过一层转发，远没有那么慢。
夸大了：多一层间接不等于必然不可用，真正要盯的是它的可用性设计而不是必然失败。
optionExplanations_en: Captures the real order of magnitude: this extra hop is typically single-digit milliseconds — far below what a user can perceive.
Overstated: minutes of delay is way beyond what pub/sub actually adds — that magnitude doesn't hold up.
Overstated: hour-scale delay is batch-processing territory; this only adds one more layer of forwarding, nowhere near that slow.
Overstated: one more layer of indirection doesn't guarantee unavailability — the real concern is how that layer is made available, not an automatic failure.

scenario: endpoint server 主要资源是打开的连接数，每条连接工作量类似。
scenario_en: The endpoint server's main resource is open connection count, and each connection does roughly similar work.
q: 负载均衡策略用什么最直观？
q_en: Which load-balancing strategy is the most direct fit?
options: 按请求的 URL path 做随机切分处理，和连接数完全无关
least connections（挑连接数最少的 server）
把所有长连接都固定发给最开始建立的那一台 server 处理
按每个请求要返回的 HTML 静态文件大小来分配后续所有连接流量
why: 连接数本身就是资源消耗的主指标。least-connections 能避免某台 server 因历史长连接过多而成为热点。
why_en: Least-connections load balancing fits endpoint servers whose main resource is open connection count.
whenOtherWins: 如果每个连接负载差异很大，还要结合消息 QPS、CPU 和 per-topic 热度。
options_en: Randomly split traffic by the request's URL path, completely unrelated to connection count.
Least connections — route to whichever server currently holds the fewest connections.
Pin all long-lived connections to whichever server handled the very first connection ever made.
Allocate all subsequent connection traffic based on the size of the HTML static file each request returns.
tradeoff: 按真实资源消耗均衡 vs 与连接数无关的路由规则
optionExplanations: URL path 和连接负载没有必然关系，按它切分完全反映不出哪台机器更忙。
连接数本身就是这里的主要资源消耗，直接挑连接数最少的 server 最直观。
固定发给第一台 server 会让它连接越攒越多，变成没人分担的热点。
静态文件大小和长连接的资源消耗没有关系，不该拿来做分配依据。
optionExplanations_en: URL path has no necessary link to connection load, so splitting by it says nothing about which server is actually busier.
Connection count is the main resource cost here, so routing to whichever server holds the fewest connections is the direct fit.
Pinning everything to the first server just lets its connections pile up into an unshared hotspot.
Static file size has nothing to do with how much a long-lived connection costs — it's the wrong signal to route on.

q: 实时系统中 zombie connection 指什么？
q_en: What is a zombie connection in a realtime system?
options: CDN 边缘节点上缓存的内容已经彻底过期失效
数据库表里出现了同一条数据的重复行
一端以为连接还活着，但另一端已经断开或清理
同一个用户同时用多台设备登录
why: 移动网络、WiFi 切换和服务器重启都可能让连接状态不一致。Heartbeat/ping-pong 用来快速发现死连接。
why_en: A zombie connection is one side believing a connection is alive after the other side has lost or cleaned it up.
options_en: Cached content at a CDN edge node has completely expired and gone stale.
Duplicate rows appearing in a database table.
One side believes the connection is still alive while the other side has already dropped or cleaned it up.
One user being logged in from multiple devices.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点的网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a network of edge servers that caches content close to users.

optionExplanations: 不成立：这是缓存内容变旧的问题，和连接两端状态是否一致无关。
不成立：这是数据一致性问题，和连接是否还活着毫无关系。
抓住定义：一端仍以为连接活着，但另一端其实已经断开或清理，这正是 zombie connection。
不成立：多设备登录是正常的会话场景，本身不构成连接故障。
optionExplanations_en: Not true: that's cached content going stale, unrelated to whether both ends of a connection agree it's still alive.
Not true: that's a data-consistency issue, unrelated to whether a connection is still alive.
The actual definition: one side still believes the connection is alive while the other side has already dropped or cleaned it up — that's a zombie connection.
Not true: logging in from multiple devices is a normal session pattern, not a connection failure by itself.
scenario: 手机用户从 WiFi 切到 4G，服务器那侧的 WebSocket 仍显示在线，消息却再也送不到。
scenario_en: A mobile user switches from WiFi to 4G; the server still shows the WebSocket as online, but messages never arrive again.

q: 断线重连设计通常需要哪些能力？（多选）
q_en: What capabilities does reconnect design usually need? (Select all that apply.)
options: heartbeat 检测断线
client reconnect with backoff
sequence number / last event ID 用来补发漏消息
断线期间消息直接丢弃且不记录
why: 真实网络一定会断。可靠实时系统要检测、重连、并根据客户端最后收到的位置补齐 gap。
why_en: Reliable realtime systems need heartbeats, reconnect backoff, and sequence IDs to replay missed updates.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server
    C->>S: heartbeat
    S-->>C: ack
    Note over C,S: 网络断开
    C->>S: reconnect + last_seq
    S-->>C: replay missed
options_en: Heartbeats detect that a connection has died.
The client reconnects with backoff to avoid a reconnect storm.
A sequence number or last event ID lets the server know what to replay.
Drop messages during a disconnect and never record them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给消息编号，客户端和服务器都能用它对齐看到哪了。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sequence number labels each message so client and server can agree on how far the client has read.

termDefinitions.meaning: SSE 事件自带的编号；重连时浏览器自动带上它，服务器据此补发漏掉的事件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Last-Event-ID is the SSE event identifier the browser resends on reconnect so the server can replay missed events.

optionExplanations: 能力：定期发 heartbeat，能比等超时更快发现连接其实已经死了。
能力：客户端带 backoff 重连，避免所有人同时重连打垮服务器。
能力：靠 sequence number/last event ID 记住客户端读到哪，重连后才知道该补发什么。
反例：直接丢弃且不记录，等于承认重连后用户会永久漏消息。
optionExplanations_en: The capability: periodic heartbeats catch a dead connection faster than waiting for a timeout.
The capability: clients reconnect with backoff so they don't all storm the server back to life at once.
The capability: a sequence number or last event ID tracks how far the client got, so reconnect knows exactly what to replay.
The failure case: dropping messages during a disconnect with no record means the user permanently loses them on reconnect.
scenario: 地铁里的聊天 App 每隔几分钟断一次网，用户重新联网后不能漏掉断线期间的消息。
scenario_en: A chat app on the subway drops connectivity every few minutes, and the user must not miss messages sent while they were offline.

scenario: WebSocket 断开 20 秒后重连，客户端需要收到断线期间的消息。
scenario_en: A WebSocket disconnects for 20 seconds and then reconnects; the client still needs the messages sent during the gap.
q: 服务端应如何支持？
q_en: How should the server support this?
options: 让客户端在成功重连之后自己凭空猜测断线期间究竟收到过什么样的消息
直接放弃处理，明确告诉用户断线期间产生的所有消息都已经永久丢失了
只依赖 TCP 协议本身在传输层自动帮你保存断线期间产生的全部消息内容
用消息队列或 Redis Streams，按序号补发错过的消息
why: WebSocket 本身不替你保存断线消息。需要可查询的消息日志和 last_seen cursor。
why_en: WebSocket reconnection needs a durable message log or queue plus a last-seen cursor to replay missed messages.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务允许丢失临时 presence/typing indicator，可以不补发这些 ephemeral events。
options_en: Let the client, after successfully reconnecting, guess out of thin air what messages it might have missed.
Simply give up and tell the user that every message sent during the disconnect is permanently lost.
Rely solely on the TCP transport layer to automatically save every message sent during a disconnect.
Use a message queue or Redis Streams and replay missed messages by sequence number.
tradeoff: 多维护一份可查询的消息日志 vs 断线期间完全无补发能力
codeSample:
XADD user:42:events * type message text "hi"
XREAD COUNT 50 STREAMS user:42:events 1699999999-0
# XADD 把事件追加进该用户的 stream
# 重连时带上 last_seen id，XREAD 从那之后读取补发

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 里的一种追加日志结构，支持按位置读取和补发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Streams is an append-only log data structure in Redis that supports reading from a given position for replay.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给消息编号，客户端和服务器都能用它对齐看到哪了。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sequence number labels each message so client and server can agree on how far the client has read.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、保证有序可靠传输的传输层协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees ordered, reliable delivery.

optionExplanations: 不成立：猜测既不可靠也不是工程方案，客户端没有任何依据知道自己错过了什么。
不成立：直接放弃会让用户体验很差，而且并不是唯一能做的选择。
不成立：TCP 只管一条连接内字节的顺序，断线后这条连接本身就没了，它不会替你持久化消息。
抓住做法：维护 per-user 的消息队列或 Redis Streams，重连后按 sequence number 从断点补发。
optionExplanations_en: Not true: guessing is neither reliable nor an engineering solution — the client has no basis for knowing what it missed.
Not true: giving up wrecks the user experience, and it isn't the only option available anyway.
Not true: TCP only orders bytes within one connection; once that connection is gone after a disconnect, it saves nothing for you.
The actual approach: keep a per-user message queue or Redis Streams, and replay from the last sequence number after reconnecting.

q: 实时系统里的 celebrity problem 是什么？
q_en: What is the celebrity problem in realtime systems?
options: 高关注用户的更新要推给百万级客户端，naive fanout 可能压垮系统
用户在设置页面填写的显示名字超过了后端字段长度限制
WebSocket 协议在设计上本身就完全无法传输任何文本或二进制类型的消息
系统里恰好所有用户账号在这一时刻都处于离线状态
why: 名人发帖、直播评论、大促库存等会制造极端 fanout。不能简单对每个 follower 单独同步推送。
why_en: The celebrity problem is massive fanout when one user's update must reach millions of clients at once.
options_en: One highly followed user's update must reach millions of clients, and naive fanout can crash the system.
The display name a user entered on the settings page exceeds the backend's field length limit.
The WebSocket protocol, by design, is fundamentally unable to transmit any text or binary type message.
Every single user account in the system happens to be offline at this exact moment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条更新要分发给大量接收者，接收者数量越大分发压力越大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fanout is delivering one update to a large number of recipients; more recipients means more delivery pressure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在一条 TCP 连接上支持客户端和服务器双向收发消息的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol that lets client and server exchange messages both ways over one persistent connection.

optionExplanations: 抓住定义：一个高关注用户一条更新就要同时推给百万级客户端，逐个同步推送会直接压垮系统。
不成立：这是字段长度校验的问题，和大规模 fanout 毫无关系。
不成立：WebSocket 文本和二进制都能传，这个说法本身就是错的。
不成立：全员离线不会造成 fanout 压力，恰恰相反是大量在线接收者才会。
optionExplanations_en: The actual definition: one highly followed user's single update must reach millions of clients at once, and naive one-by-one fanout can crash the system.
Not true: that's a field-length validation issue, unrelated to massive fanout.
Not true: WebSocket can carry both text and binary fine — that claim is simply false.
Not true: everyone being offline wouldn't create fanout pressure — it's the opposite, a huge number of online recipients that does.
scenario: 直播平台上一位 2000 万粉丝的主播开播，开播通知要同时推给所有在线粉丝。
scenario_en: On a live-streaming platform, a creator with twenty million followers goes live and the notice must reach every online follower at once.

q: 处理单个更新 fanout 给数百万用户时，可考虑哪些策略？（多选）
q_en: Which strategies can handle one update fanning out to millions of users? (Select all that apply.)
options: 缓存更新一次，通过层级/区域分发推给本地连接
批量聚合和分层广播，避免单组件直接打满
允许稍微延迟，或合并掉中间值只推最新库存
同步逐个写入所有用户连接且不做限流
why: 极端 fanout 要把压力分层、批处理或缓存。题面说库存显示允许 1–2 秒延迟、只看最新值，所以可以合并中间更新、稍晚推送，用一点新鲜度换稳定；真正的超卖保护在下单时的服务端扣减里。完全同步逐个推送会产生热点。
why_en: Extreme fanout needs layering, batching, or caching. Because the scenario says the display tolerates a 1–2 second delay and only the latest value matters, you can coalesce intermediate updates and push slightly later, trading a little freshness for stability; oversell protection lives in the server-side decrement at checkout. Fully synchronous one-by-one pushes create hotspots.
diagram:
flowchart TB
    A["热点更新"] --> B["聚合/限流"]
    B --> C["区域 fanout"]
    C --> D["Endpoint servers"]
    D --> E["大量客户端"]
options_en: Cache the update once and distribute it through regional or hierarchical layers of local connections.
Batch and broadcast hierarchically so no single component takes the full hit.
Allow slight delay, or coalesce intermediate values and push only the latest stock.
Synchronously write to every user connection one by one with no throttling.
optionExplanations: 策略：更新只算/缓存一次，再按区域或层级往下分发给本地连接，避免重复计算。
策略：批量聚合、分层广播，让压力逐层摊开，不会让单个组件直接被打满。
策略：库存显示可容忍 1–2 秒延迟，合并中间值只推最新库存，用一点新鲜度换系统稳定。
反例：同步逐个写入且不限流，正是会在百万级 fanout 下第一个被打垮的做法。
optionExplanations_en: A strategy: compute or cache the update once, then fan it out through regional or hierarchical layers to local connections, avoiding repeated work.
A strategy: batch and broadcast hierarchically so pressure spreads across layers instead of slamming one component.
A strategy: since the display tolerates a 1–2 second delay, coalesce intermediate values and push only the latest stock, trading a little freshness for stability.
The failure case: writing to every connection synchronously with no throttling is exactly what collapses first under millions-scale fanout.
scenario: 大促开场那一秒，一条库存变化要推给同时在线的 300 万个商品页连接。页面上的库存数字只做展示，允许 1–2 秒延迟、只显示最新值，真正下单时以服务端扣减结果为准。
scenario_en: At the opening second of a flash sale, one inventory change must reach three million product-page connections simultaneously. The stock number on the page is display-only: a 1–2 second delay is fine and only the latest value matters, because checkout always relies on the server-side decrement.

q: 分布式实时更新为什么会遇到 message ordering 问题？
q_en: Why do distributed realtime updates run into message ordering problems?
options: JSON 这种数据交换格式在设计上完全无法表达任何顺序字段
不同 server/partition 处理消息，发送顺序和到达顺序可能不一致
客户端在系统运行的任意时刻永远只能收到一条服务器消息
load balancer 会在转发过程中自动帮所有消息按发送时间重新排好正确顺序
why: 多个 server 并行处理时，消息可能乱序。关键流需要明确排序域和顺序来源。
why_en: Distributed realtime systems can reorder messages when different servers or paths process them concurrently.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["msg 1"] --> S1["Server A"] --> C["Client"]
    B["msg 2"] --> S2["Server B"] --> C
    S2 -.可能先到.-> C
    O["single sequencer"] -->|统一编号| C
options_en: JSON, as a data interchange format, is by design fundamentally unable to represent any ordering field.
Different servers or partitions process messages, so send order and arrival order can differ.
A client, at any moment while the system is running, can only ever receive one server message.
The load balancer automatically re-sorts every message by send time into the correct order while forwarding.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种轻量级的结构化数据格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: JSON is a lightweight structured data format.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把请求分发到多台后端服务器的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer distributes incoming requests across multiple backend servers.

optionExplanations: 不成立：JSON 完全能带一个顺序字段，格式本身不是乱序的根因。
抓住根因：不同 server/partition/网络路径并行处理，发送顺序和到达顺序天然可能对不上。
不成立：客户端能收多条消息，这个前提本身就是错的。
不成立：LB 只管转发，不会替你重排消息顺序，排序得应用层自己解决。
optionExplanations_en: Not true: JSON can easily carry an ordering field — the format itself isn't the cause of reordering.
The actual root cause: different servers, partitions, or network paths process messages in parallel, so send order and arrival order can naturally diverge.
Not true: clients can receive multiple messages — that premise is simply wrong.
Not true: a load balancer just forwards traffic, it won't reorder messages for you — ordering has to be solved at the application layer.
scenario: 聊天消息由 3 个 Kafka 分区并行消费后推给客户端，用户看到回复出现在提问前面。
scenario_en: Chat messages are consumed in parallel from three Kafka partitions before being pushed to clients, and a user sees a reply appear before the question.

scenario: 在线拍卖中，同一个 item 的出价顺序必须明确，总顺序比水平扩展更重要。
scenario_en: In an online auction, bids for the same item need a clear total order, and that order matters more than horizontal scale.
q: 更务实的排序策略是什么？
q_en: What is the more pragmatic ordering strategy?
options: 完全依赖每个客户端设备本地时钟给自己的出价打时间戳
让每一台 server 各自独立、随机决定收到消息的处理先后顺序
把同一 item 消息收拢到单个 server 打顺序号
干脆不记录任何一次出价之间的先后顺序关系
why: 产品类面试里，单 host/partition 负责同一实体通常比 vector clocks 更简单可靠。它用可控扩展换明确顺序。
why_en: For product systems, funneling one entity's messages through one server or partition gives a simple total order.
whenOtherWins: 深层基础设施或多主复制系统才更常讨论 vector clocks、logical clocks 等复杂技术。
options_en: Rely entirely on each client device's local clock to timestamp its own bids.
Let every server independently and randomly decide the processing order of messages it receives.
Funnel one item's messages through a single server that stamps a sequence number.
Simply don't record the ordering relationship between any bids at all.
tradeoff: 牺牲一点水平扩展换来简单的总顺序 vs 全局分布式排序的实现复杂度
optionExplanations: 不成立：客户端本地时钟不可信也不同步，靠它打时间戳既可能乱序也容易被作弊。
不成立：各 server 各自随机决定顺序，完全保证不了同一件商品出价的先后关系。
更务实的做法：把同一 item 的消息都收拢到一个 server/partition，由它统一打顺序号。
不成立：拍卖明确要求先后顺序，完全不记录直接违反了这个业务需求。
optionExplanations_en: Not true: a client's local clock isn't trustworthy or synchronized — timestamping bids with it invites both reordering and cheating.
Not true: each server independently randomizing processing order guarantees nothing about which bid on an item actually came first.
The pragmatic move: funnel all of one item's messages through a single server or partition that stamps a sequence number.
Not true: an auction explicitly needs bid ordering — recording none of it directly violates that requirement.

q: 什么时候才更可能讨论 vector clocks / logical timestamps？
q_en: When are vector clocks or logical timestamps more likely to come up?
options: 消息只经过单机队列顺序处理的场景
是普通在线拍卖这类产品设计题的默认首选方案
只是每 5 秒刷新一次 dashboard 数字的场景
深层分布式基础设施或多源并发更新，需要表达消息因果关系
why: 大多数产品设计题优先用单 partition 建立顺序。Vector clocks 更适合深 infra 和冲突解析。
why_en: Vector clocks are more common in deep infrastructure problems than in ordinary product realtime designs.
options_en: Messages processed sequentially through a single-machine queue.
The default first choice for an ordinary online-auction product design question.
A dashboard that just refreshes a number every five seconds.
Deep distributed infrastructure or multi-source concurrent updates that need to express causal relationships between messages.
tradeoff: 表达因果关系的通用性 vs 单 partition 方案的简单性

termDefinitions.meaning: 每台节点维护一个计数器向量，用来判断分布式事件之间的因果先后。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A vector clock is a per-node counter vector used to determine the causal order between distributed events.

scenario: 面试官追问：在线拍卖这类产品设计题里，什么情况下才真的需要引入更复杂的分布式排序机制。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks when an online-auction style product design would truly need a more complex distributed ordering mechanism.
optionExplanations: 不成立：单机队列本身顺序天然有保证，用不上 vector clock 这类跨节点因果机制。
说反了：产品设计题默认更愿意用一个 partition 就把顺序定下来，vector clocks 不是首选方案。
不成立：低频刷新的 dashboard 完全没有排序压力，谈不上要引入这类机制。
抓住场景：深层分布式基础设施或多源并发写入、需要表达因果先后时，才轮到 vector clocks 登场。
optionExplanations_en: Not true: a single-machine queue already guarantees order on its own, so there's no need for a cross-node causality mechanism like vector clocks.
Backwards: product design questions default to settling order with just one partition — vector clocks are not the first choice.
Not true: a dashboard refreshing every 5 seconds has no ordering pressure at all, so this mechanism has no reason to come up.
The actual trigger: deep distributed infrastructure or multi-source concurrent writes that need to express causal order is when vector clocks come up.

scenario: 设计 WhatsApp 类聊天：5 亿用户 × 4% 同时在线 ≈ 2000 万条长连接，还要断线补发。
scenario_en: Designing WhatsApp-style chat: 500 million users times 4 percent concurrently online is roughly 20 million live connections, plus replay after disconnects.
q: 合理主线是什么？
q_en: What is a reasonable main architecture path?
options: WebSocket 双向连接 + Pub/Sub 路由 + 消息日志支持重连补发
把所有消息汇总起来做成一份每日邮件摘要发给用户查看
让每一个用户都直接和自己的所有联系人分别建立独立的 WebRTC P2P 长连接
消息只临时存放在服务器本地内存里，完全不做任何持久化处理
why: 聊天需要双向低延迟和可靠消息。WebSocket + pub/sub + durable message log 是常见组合。
why_en: Chat commonly uses WebSockets for bidirectional delivery, pub/sub for routing, and a durable log for replay.
whenOtherWins: 低实时性通知可用 polling；端到端大群音视频才可能考虑 WebRTC。
options_en: Bidirectional WebSocket, pub/sub routing, and a message log for reconnect replay.
Roll all messages up into a daily email digest sent to the user.
Have every user open a separate, independent WebRTC peer-to-peer long-lived connection directly to each of their contacts.
Keep messages only temporarily in local server memory with absolutely no persistence.
tradeoff: 双向低延迟+可靠补发 vs 引入 Pub/Sub 和消息日志的架构复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: 在一条 TCP 连接上支持客户端和服务器双向收发消息的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol that lets client and server exchange messages both ways over one persistent connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布者把消息发到 topic，订阅该 topic 的所有客户端都会收到。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/sub, short for publish/subscribe, lets a publisher send to a topic that every subscriber of that topic receives.

termDefinitions.meaning: 支持浏览器间直接点对点音视频/数据通信的协议族。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebRTC is a protocol suite that lets browsers exchange audio, video, or data directly, peer to peer.

optionExplanations: 标准组合拳：WebSocket 提供双向低延迟送达，Pub/Sub 负责路由，消息日志撑住断线补发。
不成立：每日邮件摘要延迟以天计，完全满足不了即时聊天的送达要求。
不成立：联系人一多，每人和每个联系人各建一条 P2P 连接，连接数会爆炸式增长。
不成立：只放内存不落盘，一旦重启或断线，消息就彻底丢了。
optionExplanations_en: The standard combo: WebSocket gives bidirectional low-latency delivery, pub/sub handles routing, and a message log covers reconnect replay.
Not true: a daily email digest has day-scale delay, nowhere near what instant chat delivery needs.
Not true: with many contacts, opening a separate P2P connection to each one makes the connection count explode.
Not true: keeping messages only in memory means a restart or disconnect wipes them out for good.

scenario: Google Docs 类协作编辑要传播字符级变更、光标和选择状态，并处理冲突。
scenario_en: Google Docs-style collaborative editing must propagate character-level changes, cursors, selections, and handle conflicts.
q: 实时更新之外还必须讨论什么？
q_en: What else must be discussed beyond realtime delivery?
options: 只需要靠 CDN 缓存住文档内容就能解决并发编辑冲突
CRDT 或 OT 等冲突解决机制
把每一次字符级的变更都直接当成一张图片来上传
完全忽略掉并发编辑的先后顺序，谁的改动都会直接覆盖
why: 实时连接只解决“怎么送达”。协作编辑还要解决并发编辑冲突和文档一致性。
why_en: Collaborative editing needs realtime delivery plus conflict resolution such as CRDTs or operational transforms.
whenOtherWins: 只读 live dashboard 没有多人并发编辑冲突，不需要 OT/CRDT。
options_en: Just relying on a CDN to cache the document content is enough to solve concurrent edit conflicts.
Conflict-resolution mechanisms such as CRDTs or OT.
Treat every single character-level change as if it were an image to upload.
Completely ignore the order of concurrent edits; whoever's change lands last just overwrites the rest.
tradeoff: 实时传输解决送达 vs CRDT/OT 解决并发冲突，两者缺一不可

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种设计成可以在多个副本上并发修改、最终自动合并不冲突的数据结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CRDT, Conflict-free Replicated Data Type, is a data structure designed so concurrent edits on different replicas merge automatically without conflict.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通过变换并发操作的方式，让它们能按顺序应用而不冲突。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Operational Transformation, or OT, transforms concurrent operations so they can be applied in sequence without conflicting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点的网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a network of edge servers that caches content close to users.

optionExplanations: 不成立：CDN 缓存的是静态内容，完全解决不了两个人同时改同一段文字的冲突。
抓住要点：实时连接只管送达，并发编辑冲突还得靠 CRDT 或 OT 这类机制来合并。
不成立：图片没有可合并的结构化操作，表达不了字符级的增删改。
不成立：忽略顺序会让后一次编辑直接覆盖前一次，内容说丢就丢。
optionExplanations_en: Not true: CDN caching serves static content — it does nothing to resolve two people editing the same text at once.
The actual point: realtime delivery only gets the bytes there; merging concurrent edits still needs a mechanism like a CRDT or OT.
Not true: an image has no mergeable structured operations, so it can't represent character-level insertions and deletions.
Not true: ignoring order just lets a later edit silently overwrite an earlier one, losing content outright.

scenario: FB Live comments 中，评论量巨大，所有观众都要感到“实时”，但不一定每个人都看到每条评论。
scenario_en: In FB Live comments, comment volume is huge and every viewer should feel realtime, but not everyone must see every single comment.
q: 设计上应重点考虑什么？
q_en: What should the design focus on?
options: 把所有观众的连接都塞进单台 WebSocket server
每条评论都同步、逐个直接推给每一位观众
批处理、分层聚合和采样/过滤，避免极端 fanout 压垮系统
直接关闭评论功能来规避压力
why: 直播评论是高 fanout 高写入场景。体验上需要实时感，不一定要求每个客户端收到完整全量流。
why_en: Live comments need batching and hierarchical fanout to preserve a realtime feel without delivering every event to every viewer.
whenOtherWins: 小房间聊天可用普通 WebSocket + pub/sub，无需复杂聚合。
options_en: Put every viewer's connection on one single WebSocket server.
Synchronously push every single comment to every single viewer.
Batching, hierarchical aggregation, and sampling or filtering to avoid extreme fanout overwhelming the system.
Just disable comments entirely.
tradeoff: 牺牲“每人看到每条”的完整性 vs 保住系统在极端 fanout 下不被打垮

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条更新要分发给大量接收者，接收者数量越大分发压力越大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fanout is delivering one update to a large number of recipients; more recipients means more delivery pressure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在一条 TCP 连接上支持客户端和服务器双向收发消息的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol that lets client and server exchange messages both ways over one persistent connection.

optionExplanations: 不成立：单台 server 撑不住百万级并发连接，这不是分散压力的办法。
不成立：同步逐条推给每个人，在百万观众规模下会直接把系统打垮。
抓住重点：批处理、分层聚合、必要时采样过滤，才是应对极端 fanout 的标准做法。
不成立：关闭功能只是回避了设计问题，不是在解决 fanout 压力。
optionExplanations_en: Not true: one server can't hold millions of concurrent connections — that doesn't spread the load at all.
Not true: synchronously pushing every comment to every viewer would collapse the system at millions-of-viewers scale.
The actual focus: batching, hierarchical aggregation, and sampling or filtering where needed is the standard way to handle extreme fanout.
Not true: disabling the feature just dodges the design problem instead of solving the fanout pressure.

q: 哪些系统设计题常触发 real-time updates 模式？（多选）
q_en: Which system design questions commonly trigger the Real-time Updates pattern? (Select all that apply.)
options: WhatsApp/chat
Uber driver location
Robinhood prices/orders
Google Docs collaboration
why: 聊天、位置、行情、协作编辑、拍卖、直播评论都要求低延迟状态传播。
why_en: Chat, ride sharing, trading, and collaborative editing are common realtime update interview scenarios.
options_en: WhatsApp-style chat.
Uber driver location updates.
Robinhood live prices and orders.
Google Docs collaborative editing.
optionExplanations: 消息要即时送达每个参与者，是最经典的实时更新场景。
司机位置需要持续、高频地更新给乘客和调度系统看。
价格和订单变化要求极低延迟推给交易者，慢一点就可能造成实际损失。
字符级编辑要在多个协作者之间毫秒级同步，才不会互相覆盖。
optionExplanations_en: Messages need to reach every participant instantly — the textbook realtime-update scenario.
Driver location needs continuous, high-frequency updates pushed to riders and the dispatch system.
Price and order changes need to reach traders with very low latency, or delay can translate into real losses.
Character-level edits need millisecond-scale sync across collaborators so they don't clobber each other.
scenario: 面试只有 35 分钟，你要先挑出哪些题目里“状态变化必须秒级到达用户”是核心需求。
scenario_en: You have only 35 minutes, so first pick which questions have 'state changes must reach users within seconds' as a core requirement.

q: 为什么不要一看到“更新”就直接上 WebSocket？
q_en: Why shouldn't you jump to WebSocket as soon as you see the word "updates"?
options: 目前主流的浏览器版本都还完全不支持 WebSocket 这个协议
WebSocket 实际上完全做不到任何形式的双向通信，只能单向推送
WebSocket 无论在什么业务场景下实现和运维起来都必然会比 polling 更加简单
WebSocket 带来状态连接和部署复杂度；polling/SSE 够用时应从简单开始
why: 成熟设计会先判断实时性和双向性需求。很多状态更新每几秒刷新即可，不值得引入持久连接复杂度。
why_en: Do not jump to WebSockets unless the latency and bidirectional requirements justify stateful connection complexity.
options_en: Mainstream browser versions today still completely fail to support the WebSocket protocol.
WebSocket is actually completely incapable of any form of bidirectional communication, only one-way push.
WebSocket, no matter the business scenario, is always necessarily simpler to implement and operate than polling.
WebSocket brings stateful connections and deployment complexity, so start simple if polling or SSE is enough.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在一条 TCP 连接上支持客户端和服务器双向收发消息的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol that lets client and server exchange messages both ways over one persistent connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把请求分发到多台后端服务器的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer distributes incoming requests across multiple backend servers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 HTTP 的单向流：服务器持续推送事件，客户端只接收。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, Server-Sent Events, is an HTTP-based one-way stream where the server keeps pushing events to the client.

optionExplanations: 不成立：主流浏览器早就广泛支持 WebSocket，这不是要谨慎使用它的原因。
说反了：WebSocket 恰恰是双向的，这正是它的核心能力，不是限制。
搞反了：WebSocket 要处理连接管理、重连和 LB 改造，实现复杂度明显比 polling 高，不是更简单。
抓住理由：WebSocket 带来状态连接、重连、LB 和部署复杂度，polling/SSE 够用时应该先从简单开始。
optionExplanations_en: Not true: mainstream browsers have supported WebSocket for years — that's not a reason for caution here.
Backwards: bidirectional communication is exactly WebSocket's core capability, not a limitation it lacks.
Backwards: WebSocket has to handle connection management, reconnection, and LB changes — clearly more complex to implement than polling, not simpler.
The actual reason: WebSocket brings stateful connections, reconnection, LB, and deployment complexity — start simple with polling or SSE when that's enough.
scenario: 内部报表页的指标每 30 秒更新一次就够，团队只有 2 人，没人负责连接层运维。
scenario_en: An internal dashboard only needs its metrics refreshed every 30 seconds, and the two-person team has nobody to operate a connection tier.

q: 提出实时更新后，常见 deep dive 包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: After proposing realtime updates, what common deep dives should you expect? (Select all that apply.)
options: 断线重连和漏消息补发
单个名人/热点事件的巨大 fanout
分布式 server 下的消息排序
只讨论按钮颜色
why: 这些追问检验你是否理解实时系统的生产复杂度，而不是只会说 WebSocket。
why_en: Common realtime deep dives are reconnection, massive fanout, and message ordering.
options_en: Reconnection and replaying missed messages.
Massive fanout from one hot user or event.
Message ordering across distributed servers.
Only discussing button colors.

scenario: 聊天用 long polling，客户端与服务器单程延迟 100ms；两条消息在 10ms 内先后产生，第一条在 100ms 后到达，第二条却可能晚到 290ms。
scenario_en: A chat app uses long polling with 100 milliseconds of one-way latency; two updates happen 10 milliseconds apart, the first arrives after 100 milliseconds but the second can take up to 290.
q: 290ms 这个数字最支持哪条判断？
q_en: What design judgment does the 290 millisecond figure most support?
options: 高频更新不适合 long polling，每收一条都要重建请求
long polling 的延迟只由网络单程延迟决定，与更新到达的频率无关
把轮询间隔调成 0 就能消除这段回调间隙带来的延迟
延迟叠加只影响第一条消息，之后每条都稳定在 100ms 内
options_en: Frequent updates are a bad fit for long polling, since every message costs a fresh request.
Long polling latency is set only by one-way network latency, independent of update frequency.
Setting the polling interval to zero removes the delay in the call-back gap.
The stacking only hits the first message; every later one settles under 100 milliseconds.
why: 公式：90ms 等第一条响应送达 + 100ms 重发请求 + 100ms 拿到响应 = 290ms。更新越密，每条都要等一个请求来回，延迟就越吃亏；当这段额外延迟超出产品能接受的范围，就该考虑 SSE 或 WebSocket 这类常驻连接。
why_en: Ninety milliseconds for the first response to land, one hundred to re-issue the request, one hundred more for the reply: 290. The denser the updates, the more each one pays a full request round trip, and once that extra delay exceeds what the product tolerates, a persistent connection such as SSE or WebSocket is the better fit.
optionExplanations: 抓住含义：客户端必须收到再发起下一次请求，更新越密这段空档越吃亏。
不成立：网络延迟只贡献 100ms，另外 190ms 来自请求的收尾与重建。
搞混了：long polling 没有间隔可调，服务器本来就把请求挂着不返回。
反了：第一条恰恰是最准时的，被拖慢的是紧跟其后的那些。
optionExplanations_en: The point: the client can only issue the next request after receiving one, so denser updates lose more in that gap.
Not true: network latency contributes only 100 milliseconds; the other 190 come from finishing and rebuilding the request.
Mixed up: long polling has no interval to tune — the server already holds the request open.
Backwards: the first message is the punctual one; the ones right behind it get delayed.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: In long polling the server holds the request open until new data exists, answers, and the client immediately issues another request.
